title: よーい、アクション  (Lights, Camera, Action)

segments.t: Welcome to episode one of The Naked Director. We open in a bright Tokyo studio before jumping back to where Toru Muranishi started. Kaoru Kuroki speaks politely about living naturally and about love, while Muranishi gets his camera ready to roll. Just listen to the rhythm first without worrying about every detail.
わたくしは日本の風潮に問題があると思っております。
日本には恥じらいの文化がございます。
それに縛られる必要はございません。
でも恥ずかしいなんて思いませんよ。
あるがままに生きることが人間らしさです。
わたくしのテーマは愛でございます。
そして愛とは自然の受容でございます。
ありがとうございます。
皆さんにミラクルが起きる瞬間をお見せします。
目を閉じないでください。
いいですね？それでは参ります。
よーい、アクション！
Kuroki speaks with extra-polished studio manners, while Muranishi addresses the room like a showman. Let's hear their key lines up close.
わたくしは日本の風潮に問題があると思っております。
"'I believe there is a problem with current attitudes in Japan.' Kuroki refers to herself as " We can hear
わたくし
, a dressed-up cousin of the everyday word for 'I'. Inside her sentence,
問題
this word means problem, followed by
がある
, there is.
日本には恥じらいの文化がございます。
"'In Japan, there is a culture of shyness.' Starting with " Hear how
日本には
sets Japan up as the place we are talking about. At the end,
ございます
is an extra-polite way to say something exists.
それに縛られる必要はございません。
"'There is no need to be bound by that.' Listen for " In this line,
必要
, and this word this word means need, paired with
ございません
, the negative form that says none exists. You can use this pattern to say you do not need to do something.
でも恥ずかしいなんて思いませんよ。
"'Still, I do not feel embarrassed at all.' Opening with " The word
でも
pivots straight into 'but'.
恥ずかしい
this word means embarrassed or shy, and ending on
思いませんよ
adds a confident closing particle to press the point home.
あるがままに生きることが人間らしさです。
'Living just as you are is what makes us human.'  The speaker uses
あるがまま
paints the picture of things exactly as they are, built around
ある
, and this word this word means to be, and
生きる
this word means to live. Adding
人間らしさ
onto
人間
, and this word this word means human being, and this word turns 'human' into 'human-ness'.
わたくしのテーマは愛でございます。
"'My theme is love.' Borrowed from German, " You can catch
テーマ
this word is the everyday word for theme. After
は
, she names
愛
, and this word this word means love, and wraps up with
でございます
, a grander, stage-worthy way to say 'is'.
ありがとうございます。
"'Thank you very much.' You will hear " Here, the word
ありがとうございます
everywhere in daily life, from shops to television sets. Dropping
ございます
leaves casual
ありがとう
for friends and family.
皆さんにミラクルが起きる瞬間をお見せします。
'I will show everyone the moment a miracle happens.'  The character says
皆さん
addresses everyone in the room respectfully, and this word is built from
皆さん
, and this word this word means all, plus the polite suffix
さん
瞬間
is an instant or split second, and
お見せします
humbles the speaker while promising to show something.
目を閉じないでください。
'Please do not close your eyes.'  The phrase contains
目
is eye or eyes—the language leaves out any separate word for 'your' when body parts are obvious. Attach
ないでください
to the verb stem
閉じ
, and this word this word means to shut, whenever you want to say 'please do not'.
いいですね？
"'Are you ready?' Literally, " The phrase contains
いいですね
asks 'is it good, right?', checking that everyone is following along. A rising tone turns that short check into 'ready?' or 'got it?'.
よーい、アクション！
"'Ready, action!' Directors on Japanese sets stretch out " Here, the word
よーい
, and this word this word means preparation or 'get set', right before calling borrowed English
アクション
わたくしは日本の風潮に問題があると思っております。
日本には恥じらいの文化がございます。
それに縛られる必要はございません。
でも恥ずかしいなんて思いませんよ。
あるがままに生きることが人間らしさです。
わたくしのテーマは愛でございます。
そして愛とは自然の受容でございます。
ありがとうございます。
皆さんにミラクルが起きる瞬間をお見せします。
目を閉じないでください。
いいですね？それでは参ります。
よーい、アクション！

Notice how the formal words for 'I' and 'to be' instantly give Japanese speech a formal, public polish, while the negative request pattern gives you a clean, polite way to ask someone not to do something. Until next scene—see you again.
また会いましょう。
